definition_en: a medical condition in which excess body fat has accumulated to the point that it may harm health
core_image: 体重秤的指针压过红色刻度，腰腹堆起一圈厚厚的脂肪
scene: 社区体检的早晨，护士把软尺绕在一位中年男子的腰上，读数明显偏大。The nurse explained that obesity increases the risk of diabetes and heart disease.
sceneCN: 这里 obesity 是「肥胖症」（第 1 个义项：体脂过量并可能损害健康的疾病）；句意：护士解释说，肥胖症会增加糖尿病和心脏病的风险。

pos.zh: 肥胖症；肥胖（体脂过多的状态）

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「肥胖的」，是 obesity 的词干来源，指体脂多到影响健康
由本词 obesity 加后缀 -genic 构成，义为「致肥胖的」，形容促使人发胖的环境或食物
由本词 obesity 加后缀 -gen 构成，义为「致肥胖物质」，指被认为会促进肥胖的化学因素
由前缀 anti- 加本词构成，义为「抗肥胖的」，多用于药物与政策名称

senses.title: A clinical condition of excess body fat
senses.titleCN: 肥胖症：体脂过量的临床疾病
senses.definition: a medical condition in which excess body fat has accumulated enough to impair health, usually assessed by body mass index
senses.definitionCN: 体脂堆积到足以损害健康的疾病状态，通常用体重指数评估
senses.example: Obesity is diagnosed when the body mass index reaches thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 体重指数达到三十时即可诊断为肥胖症。
senses.why: The Latin noun obesitas named fatness; medicine turned that descriptive word into a diagnosable condition with measured thresholds.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 obesitas 本指「肥胖」，医学把这个描述性词变成可用指标界定的可诊断疾病。

senses.title: The visible state of being very overweight
senses.titleCN: 肥胖：体态上的体脂过多
senses.definition: the state of carrying much more body fat than is typical for a person of the same height and build
senses.definitionCN: 与同身高体型的人相比体脂明显过多的状态
senses.example: Her obesity made walking uphill difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 她的肥胖让上坡行走变得吃力。
senses.why: Before it was a diagnosis, the word simply described a body that had eaten itself fat, so the state sense stays closest to the original image.
senses.whyCN: 在成为诊断之前，这个词只是描述一个「吃得把自己养肥」的身体，所以状态义最贴近原初意象。

senses.title: A public health burden
senses.definition: the widespread rise of excess body fat in a population, treated as a collective public health problem
senses.definitionCN: 人群中体脂过量现象普遍上升，被视为集体性的公共卫生问题
senses.example: Childhood obesity has become a public health burden in many cities.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童肥胖在许多城市已成为公共卫生负担。
senses.why: When millions of bodies gain fat at once, the personal state becomes a collective trend that health systems must measure and manage.
senses.whyCN: 当千百万人同时发胖，个人的状态就变成卫生系统必须测量和管理的集体趋势。

intro.en: Obesity comes from Latin obesitas, meaning fatness, built on obedere, to eat away or overeat, from ob- over and edere to eat.
intro.cn: obesity 来自拉丁语 obesitas「肥胖」，由 obedere「吃掉、吃得过多」构成，其中 ob- 表「过度」，edere 表「吃」。

items.en: Edere means to eat, and it is the root behind edible and the participle obesus.
items.cn: edere 意为「吃」，是 edible 与分词 obesus 背后的词根。

items.en: Ob plus edere yields obesus, literally eaten fat, used of a person or body that is corpulent. The force of ob- here is usually taken as over or intensive.
items.cn: ob 与 edere 合成 obesus，字面是「被吃肥的」，用来形容肥胖的人或身体。这里的 ob- 一般认为表「过度」或起加强作用。

items.en: The abstract noun obesitas names fatness or corpulence, and it is the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: 抽象名词 obesitas 指肥胖或肥满，是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.en: French obésité is usually cited as a parallel route into educated English, alongside direct borrowing from Latin.
items.cn: 一般认为法语 obésité 是进入英语的另一条路径，与直接借自拉丁语的情况并存。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the early seventeenth century, at first as a general word for fatness.
items.cn: 这个名词自十七世纪初见于英语记录，最初只是泛指肥胖。

items.en: Twentieth-century medicine gave it a measured definition through body mass index, and public health made it a global epidemic.
items.cn: 二十世纪的医学用体重指数给它一个可测量的定义，公共卫生则把它变成全球性的流行问题。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective and the technical compounds built on the same Latin root; the near-meaning group holds words for excess weight that come from other roots.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根构成的形容词与技术复合词；近义组收来自其他词根的「体重过多」说法。

entries.definition: very fat in a way that harms health; the adjective behind obesity
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「肥胖的」，指体脂多到影响健康，是 obesity 的词干来源

entries.definition: describing an environment or food that promotes weight gain
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「致肥胖的」，形容促使人发胖的环境或食物

entries.definition: a chemical or other factor thought to promote obesity
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「致肥胖物质」，指被认为会促进肥胖的化学物质或其他因素

entries.definition: weighing more than is healthy; a broader and less clinical term than obesity
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「超重」，比 obesity 更宽泛，临床色彩更弱

entries.definition: the amount or degree of body fat, especially as measured in medicine
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脂肪蓄积度」，尤指医学测量中的体脂量

entries.definition: the state of being fat; an older and more formal word
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肥胖」，是较古老、较正式的说法

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root, the adjective family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根、形容词词族，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ob- means over and edere means to eat: to become obese is to eat past what the body needs.
normal.cn: ob- 表「过度」，edere 表「吃」：变胖就是吃得超过了身体所需。

normal.en: The adjective is obese, and the suffix -ity turns it into obesity, just as active becomes activity.
normal.cn: 形容词是 obese，后缀 -ity 把它变成 obesity，正如 active 变成 activity。

normal.en: Childhood obesity is the phrase used when the weight problem begins early in life.
normal.cn: childhood obesity 指体重问题在生命早期就开始出现。

normal.en: Morbid obesity is the medical label for the most severe class, where the risk is highest.
normal.cn: morbid obesity 是对最严重等级的医学称呼，此时风险最高。

normal.en: An obesogenic environment makes the healthy choice the harder one.
normal.cn: obesogenic environment 指让健康选择变得更难的环境。

abstract.en: Picture a clinic scale whose needle passes the red mark while the nurse writes a diagnosis.
abstract.cn: 想象诊所的体重秤指针越过红色刻度，护士在一旁写下诊断。

abstract.en: Picture a belt that has to be let out one notch after another.
abstract.cn: 想象腰带一格一格地往外放。

abstract.en: Picture a city map on which fast-food signs outnumber playgrounds.
abstract.cn: 想象一张城市地图，快餐招牌比操场还多。

examples.en: Obesity raises the risk of diabetes and heart disease.
examples.cn: 肥胖症会增加糖尿病和心脏病的风险。

examples.en: The clinic runs a twelve-week programme for patients with obesity.
examples.cn: 这家诊所为肥胖症患者开设了一个十二周的项目。

examples.en: Childhood obesity has risen sharply in many countries.
examples.cn: 儿童肥胖在许多国家急剧上升。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧比西提」——听上去像「哦，必死体」，只是谐音玩笑。真正的线索是 ob-（过度）+ edere（吃）：吃得过多，身体把脂肪存成了病。谐音不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 ob-（过度、越过）+ edere（吃）→ obesus（被吃肥的）→ obesitas（肥胖）→ 英语 obesity；核心义是「吃得过多，身体把多余能量存成脂肪」。ob- 在此一般认为表「过度」或起加强作用。

sensesIntro.en: Obesity begins as a measured clinical condition, extends to the visible state of a fat body, and finally names a collective public health trend.
sensesIntro.cn: obesity 从可测量的临床疾病出发，扩展到身体脂肪过多的可见状态，最后指集体的公共卫生趋势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale needle passing the red mark while fat gathers at the waist.
core.cn: 核心意象：体重秤指针越过红色刻度，脂肪堆在腰腹。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: body mass index turns fatness into a diagnosis with fixed thresholds.
branches.cn: 诊室线：体重指数把肥胖变成有固定界值的诊断。

branches.en: THE BODY: the visible state of carrying far more fat than the frame expects.
branches.cn: 身体线：身体承载的脂肪远超骨架所需，这是可见的状态。

branches.en: THE POPULATION: millions of such bodies make obesity a public health burden.
branches.cn: 人群线：千百万个这样的身体让肥胖成为公共卫生负担。

branches.en: The diagnosis measures what the body already shows.
branches.cn: 诊断测量的正是身体早已呈现的状态。

branches.en: A personal state becomes a collective trend when it spreads across a population.
branches.cn: 个人状态在人群中蔓延时，就变成集体趋势。

intro.en: Obesity is a Latin noun built from a prefix of excess and the verb for eating; English adds the adjective obese and technical compounds.
intro.cn: obesity 是由表「过度」的前缀与表示「吃」的动词构成的拉丁名词；英语再加 obese 及技术复合词加以扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin edere means to eat; ob- adds the idea of over or across, and obesus is its participle, eaten fat.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 edere 意为「吃」；ob- 加上「过度、越过」之意，obesus 是其分词，意为「被吃肥的」。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of excess to the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给动词加上「过度」的意思。

items.example: Edere is the eating root shared by edible.
items.exampleCN: edere 是与 edible 共有的「吃」词根。

items.example: Obesus describes a body that has eaten itself fat.
items.exampleCN: obesus 形容一个被吃得肥起来的身体。

items.example: Obesitas is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: obesitas 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix turns obese into obesity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 obese 变成 obesity。

items.example: Obese is the adjective that names the condition.
items.exampleCN: obese 是描述这种状态的形容词。

items.example: The suffix forms obesogenic.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 obesogenic。

items.example: An obesogenic environment favours cheap, dense food.
items.exampleCN: 致肥胖环境偏爱廉价而热量密集的食物。

items.example: Obesogens are studied as possible chemical triggers.
items.exampleCN: obesogens 被研究为可能的化学诱因。

items.example: It forms anti-obesity drugs.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 anti-obesity 这类药物名称。

definition_zh: 营养不良；营养不足；营养失衡
definition_en: a condition that results from a diet in which nutrients are too few, too many or badly balanced, so that health is harmed
core_image: 一只空碗、一副瘦削的肋骨，旁边堆着只提供热量的廉价食物
scene: 病房里，一位老人因为长期只喝粥，手臂细得能看清骨头。The dietitian noted severe malnutrition and started a high-protein feeding plan.
sceneCN: 这里 malnutrition 是「营养不良」（第 1 个义项：营养摄入不足或不均衡而损害健康）；句意：营养师注意到严重营养不良，并启动了高蛋白喂养方案。

pos.zh: 营养不良；营养不足；营养失衡

derivatives.zh: 由 mal- 加 nourish 再加 -ed 构成，义为「营养不良的」，形容长期得不到足够养分的身体
由 mal- 加名词 nourishment 构成，义为「营养不良的状态」，比 malnutrition 更强调过程与结果

senses.title: Poor nutrition in general
senses.definition: a state of poor health caused by a diet that does not supply the right amount or balance of nutrients
senses.definitionCN: 饮食提供的营养素数量或比例不当而造成的健康不良状态
senses.example: Malnutrition can result from too little food or from food of poor quality.
senses.exampleCN: 营养不良可能源于食物太少，也可能源于食物质量太差。
senses.why: The prefix mal- means bad, and nutrition is the process of nourishing the body; when that process goes wrong, the whole state is malnutrition.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 mal- 意为「坏」，nutrition 是滋养身体的过程；这个过程出了错，整个状态就是 malnutrition。

senses.title: Undernutrition: too little energy and protein
senses.titleCN: 营养不足：能量与蛋白质缺乏
senses.definition: the form of malnutrition caused by eating too little food, or too little protein and energy, over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 长期食物过少，或蛋白质与能量摄入不足所造成的一类营养不良
senses.example: Severe malnutrition leaves children too weak to fight infection.
senses.exampleCN: 严重的营养不足使孩子虚弱得难以抵抗感染。
senses.why: The most visible branch of the word is simple scarcity: the body receives less fuel and building material than it burns and repairs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最可见的分支就是单纯的匮乏：身体得到的燃料与建筑材料少于它消耗和修补所需。

senses.title: Micronutrient deficiency
senses.definition: malnutrition caused by a lack of specific vitamins or minerals, even when enough calories are eaten
senses.definitionCN: 即使热量足够，因特定维生素或矿物质缺乏而造成的营养不良
senses.example: Iron-deficiency anaemia is a common form of malnutrition in young women.
senses.exampleCN: 缺铁性贫血是年轻女性中常见的营养不良形式。
senses.why: Mal- does not only mean too little food; it means wrong nourishment, so a diet full of calories but empty of iron still counts.
senses.whyCN: mal- 不只表示食物太少，还表示「滋养得不对」，所以热量充足却缺铁的饮食仍算营养不良。

senses.title: Imbalance, including excess
senses.definition: the broad public health sense in which malnutrition includes both undernutrition and overweight caused by energy-dense diets
senses.definitionCN: 公共卫生的广义用法，营养不良同时包括营养不足与高能量饮食引起的超重
senses.example: Health workers now speak of malnutrition in countries where obesity is also common.
senses.exampleCN: 如今卫生工作者在肥胖同样常见的国家也会谈到营养不良。
senses.why: Modern public health defines the word by outcome rather than by scarcity: any diet that damages health through its nutrients is malnutrition.
senses.whyCN: 现代公共卫生按结果而非匮乏来定义这个词：任何因营养素而损害健康的饮食都算营养不良。

intro.en: Malnutrition joins the Latin prefix mal-, meaning bad, to nutrition, from Latin nutrire, to nourish.
intro.cn: malnutrition 由拉丁语前缀 mal-「坏」与 nutrition 组合而成，后者来自拉丁语 nutrire「滋养」。

items.en: Malus means bad or evil, and its prefix form mal- marks a thing or process as wrong or defective.
items.cn: malus 意为「坏的、恶的」，其前缀形式 mal- 给事物或过程打上「错误、有缺陷」的标记。

items.en: Nutrire means to nourish or feed; it also gives nutrient, nutritious and nutrition.
items.cn: nutrire 意为「滋养、喂养」，还生出 nutrient、nutritious 与 nutrition。

items.en: The noun nutritio names the act of nourishing, and English nutrition descends from it through French.
items.cn: 名词 nutritio 指滋养的行为，英语 nutrition 经由法语承自它。

items.en: French is generally credited with joining mal- to nutrition in the nineteenth century, though the exact first use is not fully settled.
items.cn: 一般认为法语在十九世纪把 mal- 与 nutrition 组合起来，但确切的首次使用尚无定论。

items.en: English adopted the word in the nineteenth century, as doctors began to describe deficiencies caused by poor diet.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪引入该词，当时医生开始描述劣质饮食造成的缺乏症。

items.en: Twentieth-century nutrition science split it into undernutrition and micronutrient deficiency, and later added the double burden of excess weight.
items.cn: 二十世纪的营养科学把它分为营养不足与微量营养素缺乏，后来又加上超重与不足并存的双重负担。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the nourishing root or on mal-; the near-meaning group gathers terms for shortages of food and specific nutrients.
note.cn: 形近组收围绕「滋养」词根或 mal- 构成的词；近义组收食物与特定营养素短缺的说法。

entries.definition: badly nourished over time, so that health and growth suffer
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「营养不良的」，指长期得不到足够养分而健康与生长受损

entries.definition: the state or result of being badly nourished
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「营养不良的状态或结果」，比 malnutrition 更强调过程

entries.definition: the process of getting and using the food needed for health; the base noun inside malnutrition
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「营养、滋养过程」，是「malnutrition」内部的基础名词

entries.definition: the form of poor nutrition caused by too little food or too few nutrients
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「营养不足」，专指食物或营养素过少造成的营养不良

entries.definition: a shortage of a substance the body needs, such as a vitamin or mineral
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺乏、不足」，指身体所需物质（如维生素或矿物质）的短缺

entries.definition: extreme suffering or death from lack of food; the most severe end of the scale
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「饥饿、饿死」，指因缺乏食物而极度受苦甚至死亡，是程度最重的一端

normalIntro.en: The prefix mal- and the nourishing root nutrire are the two handles this word gives you.
normalIntro.cn: 前缀 mal- 与表示「滋养」的词根 nutrire，是这个词给你的两个把手。

normal.en: Mal- means bad: malnutrition is bad nourishment, not simply little food.
normal.cn: mal- 意为「坏」：malnutrition 是「糟糕的滋养」，不只是食物少。

normal.en: Nutrire means to nourish, and the same root gives nutrient, nutrition and nutritious.
normal.cn: nutrire 意为「滋养」，同一词根还给出 nutrient、nutrition 与 nutritious。

normal.en: Severe acute malnutrition is the emergency form that needs therapeutic feeding.
normal.cn: severe acute malnutrition 是需要治疗性喂养的急症形式。

normal.en: Protein-energy malnutrition names the shortage of both fuel and building material.
normal.cn: protein-energy malnutrition 指燃料与建筑材料同时短缺。

normal.en: A malnutrition screening tool is used on admission to find patients at risk.
normal.cn: malnutrition screening 工具在入院时用来找出高风险病人。

abstract.en: Picture a body as a house whose supply of bricks, fuel and workers has all gone wrong at once.
abstract.cn: 想象身体像一座房子，砖块、燃料和工人的供应同时出了错。

abstract.en: Picture the arm of a child that is thinner than the wrist of an adult.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子的手臂比成年人的手腕还细。

abstract.en: Picture a plate piled with rice but without a single green leaf or piece of meat.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘堆满白饭、却没有一片绿叶或一块肉的饭菜。

examples.en: Malnutrition slows growth and weakens immunity in young children.
examples.cn: 营养不良会延缓幼儿生长并削弱免疫力。

examples.en: The hospital screens every patient for malnutrition on admission.
examples.cn: 这家医院在每位病人入院时都做营养不良筛查。

examples.en: Iron deficiency is a hidden form of malnutrition in many rich countries.
examples.cn: 缺铁在许多富裕国家是一种隐蔽的营养不良形式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「玛纽吹申」——听成「马牛吹神」只是谐音玩笑。真正的线索是 mal-（坏）+ nutrire（滋养）：滋养的方式出了错，就是营养不良。谐音不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 mal-（坏、错误）+ nutrire（滋养）→ nutrition（滋养）→ 法语 malnutrition → 英语 malnutrition；核心义是「滋养的方式出了错」，既包括不足，也包括比例失衡。

sensesIntro.en: Malnutrition runs from the general state of bad nourishment, through shortage of energy and protein, through lack of specific micronutrients, to the broad public health sense that also includes excess.
sensesIntro.cn: malnutrition 从「滋养不当」的总称，经能量与蛋白质不足、特定微量营养素缺乏，一直到也包含营养过剩的公共卫生广义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl that holds calories but lacks what a body needs to build and repair itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只盛着热量、却缺少身体修补材料的碗。

branches.en: THE GENERAL STATE: any diet that nourishes the body badly produces malnutrition.
branches.cn: 总称线：任何滋养不当的饮食都会造成营养不良。

branches.en: THE SHORTAGE: too little energy and protein is the classic and most visible form.
branches.cn: 匮乏线：能量与蛋白质过少是最典型、最可见的形式。

branches.en: THE MICRONUTRIENT: enough calories with missing vitamins or minerals is still malnutrition.
branches.cn: 微量线：热量足够但维生素或矿物质缺失，仍属营养不良。

branches.en: THE DOUBLE BURDEN: public health now counts overweight and undernutrition under one word.
branches.cn: 双重线：公共卫生如今把超重与营养不足都归入同一个词。

branches.en: The outcome, not the amount of food, decides whether a diet counts as malnutrition.
branches.cn: 决定一种饮食是否算营养不良的，是结果，而不是食物总量。

intro.en: Malnutrition is a French-built word: the prefix mal- and the Latin nourishing root nutrire, with English keeping the noun unchanged.
intro.cn: malnutrition 是法语构成的词：前缀 mal- 与拉丁语「滋养」词根 nutrire，英语原样保留了这一名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin malus means bad, nutrire means to nourish, and nutritio is the noun for the act of nourishing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 malus 意为「坏」，nutrire 意为「滋养」，nutritio 则是表示滋养行为的名词。

items.example: The prefix marks a process that has gone wrong.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记一个出了错的过程。

items.example: Malus is the source of the prefix mal-.
items.exampleCN: malus 是前缀 mal- 的来源。

items.example: Nutrire is the root of nutrition and nutrient.
items.exampleCN: nutrire 是 nutrition 与 nutrient 的词根。

items.example: Nutritio became nutrition in English.
items.exampleCN: nutritio 在英语中变成 nutrition。

items.example: Nutrition is the base noun inside malnutrition.
items.exampleCN: nutrition 是 malnutrition 内部的基础名词。

items.example: Nutrients are what a poor diet fails to supply.
items.exampleCN: 营养素正是劣质饮食供应不足的东西。

items.example: A nutritious diet prevents malnutrition.
items.exampleCN: 有营养的饮食能预防营养不良。

items.example: Malnourished children need therapeutic food.
items.exampleCN: 营养不良的儿童需要治疗性食品。

items.example: The suffix builds nouns such as nutrition.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 nutrition 这类名词。

definition_zh: 脱水；失水；干燥；脱水反应
definition_en: the loss or removal of water from the body, a material or a chemical compound
core_image: 一片干裂的土地，最后一道水痕在裂缝边缘消失
scene: 夏夜的急诊室里，一位长跑者被扶进来，嘴唇干裂，皮肤捏起后迟迟不回弹。The doctor diagnosed dehydration after two hours of running in the heat.
sceneCN: 这里 dehydration 是「脱水」（第 1 个义项：身体失水达到影响功能的程度）；句意：医生诊断他在高温中跑了两小时后出现了脱水。

pos.zh: 脱水；失水；干燥；（化学）脱水反应

derivatives.zh: 由本词逆构而成的动词，义为「脱水；使干燥」，也可指身体失去水分
由 dehydrate 加 -ed 构成，义为「脱水的；干燥的」，常形容病人或食品
由 dehydrate 加 -or 构成，义为「脱水器；干燥机」，指去除水分的设备
由前缀 re- 加本词构成，义为「补液；复水」，指把失去的水补回去

senses.title: Water loss from the body
senses.definition: a condition in which the body loses more water than it takes in, so that normal functions are disturbed
senses.definitionCN: 身体失去的水多于摄入的水，正常功能因此受到干扰的状态
senses.example: Dehydration can cause dizziness, thirst and dark urine.
senses.exampleCN: 脱水可能引起头晕、口渴和尿色加深。
senses.why: The prefix de- means removal, and the Greek root for water is hydor; medicine names the state by what has been taken out of the body.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 de- 表示「去除」，希腊语中「水」的词根是 hydor；医学用「被从身体里拿走了什么」来命名这种状态。

senses.title: The process of removing water
senses.titleCN: 脱水；干燥：去除水分的过程
senses.definition: the process of removing water from food, soil or another material in order to preserve or dry it
senses.definitionCN: 为保存或干燥而从食物、土壤等材料中去除水分的过程
senses.example: Food dehydration preserves vitamins that heat would destroy.
senses.exampleCN: 食品脱水能保留住受热会被破坏的维生素。
senses.why: The same removal image leaves the body: drying fruit or soil is dehydration in its plainest mechanical sense.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「去除」意象离开身体：把水果或土壤弄干，就是 dehydration 最朴素的机械义。

senses.title: A chemical reaction that removes water
senses.definition: a chemical reaction in which a molecule loses water, or in which two molecules join while a water molecule is released
senses.definitionCN: 分子失去水，或两个分子结合时释放出一个水分子的化学反应
senses.example: Dehydration of ethanol at high temperature produces ethene.
senses.exampleCN: 乙醇在高温下脱水生成乙烯。
senses.why: Chemistry generalised the removal: water is not only dried away but taken out of the structure of a molecule, and the word follows the same logic.
senses.whyCN: 化学把「去除」一般化：水不只是被晾干，而是从分子结构中被取走，词义沿用同一逻辑。

intro.en: Dehydration combines Latin de-, away from, with the Greek word for water, hydor, and the noun suffix -ation.
intro.cn: dehydration 由拉丁语前缀 de-「离开」、希腊语表示「水」的 hydor，以及名词后缀 -ation 组合而成。

items.en: Hydor is the Greek word for water; it also gives hydrology, hydrogen and hydrate.
items.cn: hydor 是希腊语「水」，它还生出 hydrology、hydrogen 与 hydrate。

items.en: The Latin prefix de- means away from or down, and here it marks removal.
items.cn: 拉丁语前缀 de- 意为「离开、向下」，在这里表示「去除」。

items.en: Nineteenth-century chemistry built the noun from de- and hydor to name the loss of water from a compound; the exact first use is not fully settled.
items.cn: 十九世纪化学用 de- 与 hydor 造出这个名词，指化合物失去水；确切的首次使用尚无定论。

items.en: English adopted it first in chemistry and then extended it to physiology and clinical medicine.
items.cn: 英语先在化学中采用，随后扩展到生理学与临床医学。

items.en: Today the medical sense dominates: dehydration means the water deficit of the body, and rehydration is its treatment.
items.cn: 如今医学义占主导：dehydration 指身体的水亏欠，rehydration 则是它的处理办法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the verb, the adjective and the prefixed partner of dehydration; the near-meaning group holds thirst, fluid loss and technical drying words.
note.cn: 形近组收 dehydration 的动词、形容词与加前缀的对应词；近义组收口渴、体液丢失与技术性的干燥说法。

entries.definition: to remove water from something, or to lose water from the body
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「脱水、使干燥」，也可指身体失去水分

entries.definition: having lost water; used of patients, food and other materials
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「脱水的、干燥的」，常用于病人、食品与材料

entries.definition: the act of restoring water that has been lost
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补液、复水」，指把失去的水补回去

entries.definition: the feeling of needing water; a signal of dehydration rather than the state itself
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「口渴」，是脱水的信号，而不是脱水状态本身

entries.definition: loss of body fluid, a broader term because it includes water and salts
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「体液丢失」，范围更宽，因为同时包括水分与盐分

entries.definition: thorough drying, especially in scientific or geological use
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「彻底干燥」，多用于科学或地质语境

normalIntro.en: The prefix de-, the Greek water root hydor and the clinical partner rehydration are the handles for this word.
normalIntro.cn: 前缀 de-、希腊语「水」词根 hydor，以及临床上的对应词 rehydration，是这个词的把手。

normal.en: De- means away: dehydration is water taken away from something.
normal.cn: de- 意为「离开」：dehydration 就是水被从某物中拿走。

normal.en: Hydor is Greek for water, and the same root appears in hydrate and hydrogen.
normal.cn: hydor 是希腊语「水」，同一词根还出现在 hydrate 与 hydrogen 中。

normal.en: Severe dehydration is the emergency phrase; it calls for fluids by mouth or by vein.
normal.cn: severe dehydration 是急症说法，需要口服或静脉补液。

normal.en: Signs of dehydration include thirst, dark urine and skin that stays pinched.
normal.cn: signs of dehydration 包括口渴、尿色深和捏起后不回弹的皮肤。

normal.en: Rehydration is the treatment: the same water put back.
normal.cn: rehydration 是治疗办法：把同样的水补回去。

abstract.en: Picture cracked lips and a tongue stuck to the roof of the mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象干裂的嘴唇和贴在口腔上颚的舌头。

abstract.en: Picture a slice of apple left in the sun until it turns to leather.
abstract.cn: 想象一片苹果留在太阳下，直到变得像皮革一样。

abstract.en: Picture a molecule letting go of a tiny water bead as two parts join.
abstract.cn: 想象一个分子在两个部分结合时放出一颗小水珠。

examples.en: Athletes lose water quickly, and dehydration can impair performance within an hour.
examples.cn: 运动员失水很快，脱水能在一小时内削弱运动表现。

examples.en: The nurse watched for signs of dehydration in the feverish child.
examples.cn: 护士留意那个发烧孩子身上的脱水征象。

examples.en: Dehydration of the sample left a fine white powder.
examples.cn: 样品脱水后留下了一种细白的粉末。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「滴嗨追申」——听成「滴、嗨、追」只是谐音联想。真正的线索是 de-（去除）+ hydor（水）：把水拿走，就是脱水。谐音不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 de-（离开、去除）+ 希腊语 hydor（水）→ 近代科学拉丁语 dehydration（失水）→ 英语 dehydration；核心义是「把水从某物中拿走」，医学上指身体失水，化学上指分子失去水。

sensesIntro.en: Dehydration starts as a medical state of water deficit, becomes the general process of drying, and ends as a chemical reaction that removes water from a molecule.
sensesIntro.cn: dehydration 从身体缺水这一医学状态出发，扩展为一般的干燥过程，最后指从分子中取走水的化学反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water leaving a surface until only cracks and dry edges remain.
core.cn: 核心意象：水从表面离去，只剩裂缝与干边。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: water lost faster than it is replaced becomes a measurable fluid deficit.
branches.cn: 临床线：失水快于补水，就形成可测量的液体亏欠。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: drying food or soil is the same removal without a body.
branches.cn: 过程线：干燥食物或土壤，是同样的去除，只是没有身体参与。

branches.en: THE MOLECULE: chemistry takes water out of a compound and keeps the name.
branches.cn: 分子线：化学从化合物中取走水，仍沿用这个名字。

branches.en: Both the clinical state and the drying process are defined by water that is no longer there.
branches.cn: 临床状态与干燥过程都由「已经不在那里的水」来定义。

branches.en: From a drying room to a reaction flask, the word follows the same act of removal.
branches.cn: 从干燥间到反应瓶，这个词追随着同一个「去除」动作。

intro.en: Dehydration joins a Latin prefix of removal to a Greek water root, a mixed origin that English kept intact.
intro.cn: dehydration 把表「去除」的拉丁前缀与希腊语「水」词根结合在一起，英语原样保留了这种混合来源。

latinIntro.en: De- is Latin for away or down; hydor is Greek for water, and the noun suffix -ation is Latin.
latinIntro.cn: de- 是拉丁语「离开、向下」；hydor 是希腊语「水」，名词后缀 -ation 则来自拉丁语。

items.example: The prefix signals that water is being taken away.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示水正被取走。

items.example: Hydor is the water root of the word.
items.exampleCN: hydor 是这个词的「水」词根。

items.example: The combining form hydr- appears in hydrate.
items.exampleCN: 构词形式 hydr- 出现在 hydrate 中。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成表示过程的名词。

items.example: Dehydrate is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: dehydrate 是这个词名词形式背后的动词。

items.example: Dehydrated patients need fluids.
items.exampleCN: 脱水的病人需要补液。

items.example: A dehydrator dries fruit at low heat.
items.exampleCN: 干燥机用低温把水果烘干。

items.example: Dehydrating food is a way to store it longer.
items.exampleCN: 把食物脱水是一种延长保存时间的办法。

items.example: Re- plus hydration gives rehydration.
items.exampleCN: re- 加上 hydration 构成 rehydration。

items.example: Oral rehydration saves lives in severe cases.
items.exampleCN: 口服补液在重症病例中能挽救生命。
